blog_material: THE HEADLINE, corrected (#95 + PR #89): on the seeded T1c webapp repair cell, local Gemma 4 E4B QAT lands AND in-run verifies the fix 20/20, but the harness only lets it CLAIM success 9/20 — the other 11 are recorded `exhausted`. Mechanism is harness machinery (askme.py:3113-3130, second consecutive repeat of an already-successful shell hard-terminates the attempt), not model capability. This is a sharper and more interesting result than a bare 45% completion rate. Do NOT repeat the issue's 'done is emitted zero times' line — refuted.

THE INVERSE-FAILURE PAIR (PR #89, same task family, same harness): hosted gpt-oss-20b@low reported T1c complete without touching the protected test and held-out acceptance caught /health still returning {'status':'down'} (false completion); local E4B did the repair correctly and could not claim it (false exhaustion). Both surfaced by independent acceptance rather than agent self-report. This is the best single argument for the held-out-acceptance design.

REGISTERED NULL RESULT DONE RIGHT (#31): preregistered protocol with declared cells, 10 trials/arm, alpha=0.05, two-sided rule, AND mediators. Result heuristic 4/10 vs lifecycle 5/10, Fisher p=1.000. The 4-run pilot's apparent effect (0/4 vs 2/3) and its ~70% wall-time penalty both evaporated at n=10. The mediators showed the lifecycle guards fired ZERO times and the cell never tested the mechanism — a measurement that would have been invisible without preregistering mediators. The owner also logs his own hypothesis as falsified and discloses three contaminated trials with a sensitivity analysis.

MID-EXPERIMENT SELF-CORRECTION (PR #97): the PEG probe's naive ok flag conflated a grammar defect with hitting the 512-token cap; fixed in a separate analyze.py rather than by rewriting the probe, so the committed script provably produced the committed records. Result: 0/64 parser failures — llama.cpp #25986 did not reproduce on this cell — recorded as a bounded negative with four named limits, including that arm C never provoked its own condition (16/16 declined), so the missing-escape defect is 'untested, not cleared'.

CONCRETE HONEST CONSTRAINT (PR #97): the legacy 512-token write cap binds on ordinary write work — 4/16 trials hit it, 2 mid-string — while 0/16 capped at 2048 tokens with payloads to 5,507 chars. Defensible, dated, cell-scoped.

'WE REMOVED THE THINGS THAT LET THE HARNESS LIE' (#68, fully substantiated in code): repetition never proves acceptance; exhaustion is terminal with no shell-success reconciliation (askme.py:3840-3852); an unavailable or malformed validator yields typed `complete_unverified`, not a pass (askme.py:3801-3803); budgets come from named capability profiles, never from provider names (askme.py:109-211).

A REAL LONG-RUN OPS BUG WITH A RETAINED RECORD (commit 6ac9788): two E25 build walls of 5791.9s and 16607.2s against a 1200s cap, caused by agent-spawned descendants surviving the harness's subprocess kill and holding inherited pipes open. Good 'what actually breaks unattended' anecdote — and a reason no E25 hard-suite wall-clock number may be quoted as performance data.

EVOLUTION FRAMING for #94 (only honest option if not fixed first): 'the sentinel transport solved escaping and truncation salvage; native tool calls made the escaping half obsolete and cost us the salvage half — that is issue #94.' Pairs well with the E25 paired bench. Do NOT present resume-anchor recovery as a current capability.

LIVE AND FULLY HONEST TODAY: bounded read/search/tree truncation integrity with `truncation_reasons` carried through action result, model history and JSONL (actions.py:727/781/1162). That half of the truncation story can be told as-is.

AFTER MERGING PR #96, the true CI claim is: 'the deterministic suite runs green on real Apple Silicon macOS (3.10 and 3.14), and the llama.cpp local backend is contract-checked end to end on a hosted M1 — Homebrew llama.cpp installs, llama-server serves, AskMe's real client decodes a native tool call' (job 99209228350: 'PROBE OK: decoded a native tool call'). NOT claimable: that CI reproduces the M1 Gemma 4 E4B setup — no hosted GitHub runner is both Apple Silicon and >=16 GB, and the reference lane has never executed.

ACCURATE NEGATIVE CASE STUDY already in-repo (docs/PERFORMANCE.md:711+): FeatureBench v6, one external real-repo task, one attempt per model — Gemma 11/13 F2P, Qwen 7/13, patches that apply but do not resolve, planning exhaustion, no delivered-test execution. Strong material, but must carry the interface-revision caveat (see corrections).

CAVEATS THE POST MUST CARRY: single task / single model / single machine on every local number; n=1 or n=3 per hosted cell under automatic provider routing (not reliability rates); 'not a sandbox' verbatim from CLAUDE.md and docs/SECURITY.md; the 9/9 C-header result and the fix_missing_include 609s->15.7s speedup are partly a hard-coded two-header deterministic template firing (issue #68 comment 5173710492; PERFORMANCE.md's 'zero recovery machinery invoked' was wrong and was corrected by PR #87).
